title: The mission stub names two outcome values the product does not have
foundBy: user report (host), reading the scaffolded comments: "they seem very esoteric, stated as if some obscure concepts must be pre-known"

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestScaffoldPromptsDoNotInventVocabulary -count=1: PASS. Proved by mutation: putting `Met` back into the mission stub fails it by name. End to end, init's closing output now names the playbook, and MANUAL's sample of that output matches the binary, which SURF-303 checks. make check exit 0.

resolution: The mission stub carries no outcome value. It says the orchestrator ends with one of four, that every one but success names what is unmet, and sends the reader to the playbook for the list. Deleting the vocabulary rather than correcting it removes the surface the drift came from. TestScaffoldPromptsDoNotInventVocabulary refuses a stub that spells one again.
details:
`init` scaffolds a mission whose comments name outcomes that do not exist.

The stub calls the definition of done "what an outcome of `Met` will be judged against". It also names "a `Converged` report" that must name gaps relative to it. The product has four values and neither of those is among them. `protocol.Outcomes` is `campaign-met`, `campaign-converged`, `campaign-exhausted` and `campaign-blocked`.

An author writes the mission against the vocabulary the stub gave them, and meets the real one when reading the campaign's verdict at the end. The two outcomes the stub omits are the two an operator most needs to tell apart. Whether effort was ever the problem separates `campaign-exhausted` from `campaign-blocked`, and each implies a different move.

The drift has a cause worth fixing rather than patching. The stub restates a vocabulary that is defined elsewhere, so it can disagree with it. PLAYBOOK carries the four values in a table with what each means for the operator, and MANUAL carries them too. Nothing held the stub against either.

The same pass should reach the comments around it. They allude to concepts an author has not met. One names an obligation as irreversible rather than saying that uncommitted work dies with the machine. Another calls a brief standing context without introducing the term.

notes.text: Superseded in part by SAC-022. The comments this record improved are gone, because the stubs that carried them are gone. What survives is the guidance itself, now in the playbook under the headings a brief uses.
